## Submitting to the chart {#getting-your-dot-on-the-chart-route-2}

You submit twice, and the two are different in kind. Both routes use the same function names.

**Task 4 – the exploratory dot (open circle).** Nothing is committed here.

1. **`try_spec(...)`** – one argument per axis, every one defaulting to the baseline you reproduced. `try_spec(estimator = "pooled_cl")` changes one thing and leaves the rest alone.
2. **`my_experiments()`** – prints everything you have tried so far, side by side, with only the axes that actually varied.
3. **`submit_exploration()`** – sends the most recent try to the chart, labelled as exploration. Open the printed link and press **Send**.

**Task 5 – the declared dot (filled circle).** Now the choice binds.

4. **Preregister.** Make one choice on every axis in the preregistration cell (`claim_align <- TRUE` is already set for you), then run `prereg()`. That declaration is your commitment – copy the whole cell into your notes.
5. **`build_model(...)`** – write your specification as a formula. It accepts only code that matches your preregistration and tells you what is off when it does not.
6. **`run_spec(my_model)`** – computes your specification and shows the coefficient, its claim-aligned partial *r* (below zero supports the claim), and your placement against the canonical 840-spec grid.
7. **`report_result()`** – no arguments. It builds your submission from the preregistration and prints a clickable, pre-filled form link; open it and press **Send**.

If any of that stalls, work the ladder below.

---

## A stalled browser lab

The browser lab runs R inside your browser tab, and browsers occasionally baulk. Work down this list. Each rung is more certain than the one before, and rung 4 gets you a dot on the chart no matter what your machine does.

1. **Hard reload, then rerun.** Reload the page clearing the cache (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R), wait for R to restart, and **rerun the chunks above** the one that failed – webR needs the earlier chunks to have run in this session before a later one will work.
2. **Switch browser.** If a chunk still will not run, open the browser lab in a different browser (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox). A fresh browser clears most stubborn webR problems.
3. **Follow the shared screen – the 'buddy chunk'.** If your machine simply will not cooperate, watch the facilitator run the exact chunk on the shared screen and read your numbers from there. You miss no step by doing this.
4. **Read your numbers to the facilitator.** If `run_spec()` or `report_result()` printed your result but the form link will not open – or a cell simply refuses to run – read the printed `b`, `se`, `t` (or `z` for a beta family), `df`, `n` and claim-aligned `r` to the facilitator, who lands the dot for you. The lab has already applied the claim-alignment convention, so there is nothing to convert, and no working form link is needed at your end.

::: {.callout-note}
## The by-hand grid lookup
Last resort, facilitator-side, if a participant's cells will not run at all: every menu specification is a row in one of the files under `data/grid/`. The file is named by the six Level 1 choices joined with double underscores, in the order outcome, predictor, co-predictor, estimator, sample, weights – the baseline is `mcosmo__unemp__none__fe_twoway__all__none.csv.gz` – and the row inside it is picked by the eight Level 2 and Level 3 choices (`construction`, `noop`, `item_set`, `cell_weight`, `measure`, `pred_form`, `family`, `se`). A beta-family row reports `z` in place of `t`. Read off `b`, `se`, `t`/`z`, `df` and `n`, and take `r` from the `r_ca` column, which is already claim-aligned. Then apply the flips that the lab applies automatically to `b` and `t`/`z` only: reverse their sign for a negative framing (`mcomm`, `mlib`, `mneg`), and again for a GDP-growth predictor. Enter those into the [form]({{< var results-form-url >}}); the dot lands without anything being fitted.
:::

## IDE quick fixes

| If ... | Then ... |
|---|---|
| A package will not load, or `feols` / `plm` is "not found" | Run the checker again – `source("R/check_setup.R")` – and let it install what is missing; or install by hand, e.g. `install.packages("fixest")`. |
| The `renv` / `pak` restore stalls or half-finishes | Restart R (Session menu), then run the restore again; a second pass usually completes what the first left. |
| "Permission denied" while installing a package | Let R use a personal library it can write to – accept the offer from R to create a personal library, then reinstall. |
| A data file is "not found" | Check you opened the unzipped **folder** in your IDE (File → Open Folder in Positron and VS Code; the `.Rproj` file in RStudio), not a single file – the paths in the code are relative to that folder. |
| Something not listed here | The [setup help page](../help.qmd) has the longer table, with links to the discussions where each problem was solved, and prompts to give an AI assistant. |
| Everything is stuck | Open the [browser lab](browser-lab.qmd) and carry on there. You lose nothing required. |

## Rendering the report {#rendering-your-report-route-1}

Render your report so your preregistration block is written down and timestamped before you run your specification. In Positron and in RStudio, press the **Render** button at the top of the open report; in VS Code, run the Quarto extension's Render command; or run `quarto render index.qmd` in a terminal inside any of them. On the browser lab page the same block lives in the page and updates in the tab.
